title: Group Internal Lines | Clo 2025.1 Features Deep Dive
description:
The new update to our hardware in CLO 2025.1 allows you to quickly group internal lines using shortcuts, with grouping preserved during pattern edits.

Check out other new features here:https://clo3d.com/en/clo/features

Questions? Comment below or ask in our CLO discord server: https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/7814962429977-How-can-I-join-CLO-Discord?utm_campaign=multi_item_banner_JointheOfficialCLODiscord&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=later-linkinbio

transcript: Hey everyone, it's Phoebe here, and I have some great updates to share with you for our internal lines. So let's dive on in and have some fun while we learn. Okay, so here I have my 2D window, and I'm going to show you some fun updates we have with our internal lines. First thing is the improvement to grouping. So with my transform pattern tool selected, shortcut A, I can select my two internal lines holding down shift, and then right-clicking right on top of them, you could always get to group, and then you can group the internal lines. But now we have that shortcut where you can just select these two holding down shift and then hit Control-G. For Max, it'd be Command-G. Then once you're done grouping, you can select your internal lines. Once they're selected and grouped, you can see that now you can move them around, and they'll all be grouped together. They'll keep the grouping even if you decide to, like, cut this right here. So if I decide to cut this pattern, the grouping will still stay, as you can see. And even if I decide to re-merge this together, they're grouping will stay. The only way that it's not going to group is if you select it, right-click, and ungroup them. Pretty cool. Now, another really cool update we've done with the internal lines is with this center line. Now you can extend it to that center line. Going to your Edit Pattern tool, you can then select the internal line, right-click right on top of it, and then extend to Trim, and then you can say to Unfolded Line. And then it will extend to the Unfolded Line. And you can see that there's only one internal line, and it's great. It will not work with Add Point. Like, if I select this, right-click, Extend slash Trim to Add Point, it's not going to be there. That's because you cannot add a point. To that center line, right? Because you can only add segment points to pattern outlines, and the center line is not a pattern outline. So that's why that doesn't work. It makes sense. But you can, of course, go to Extend slash Trim, and then to Unfolded Line. We also added this if you decided to distribute. So if I went to my back pattern here and selected these two pattern outlines, right-clicked on top and said, Distribute Internal Line Between Segments, I then have an option right here, Extend to Unfolded Line. And then it will extend to this half. I can then increase, right? I can also say I want it to be a straight line, anything like that. And then I can hit OK. And then the other one will be created. So really great and helpful. Okay. Thanks. Bye. For questions, any questions use that Comment section down below. Don't forget to like and subscribe. There's tons of great videos to help you out in your CLO journey. Keep having fun in CLO. And thanks again. Bye. Bye. Bye. Bye. Bye. Bye. Bye. Bye. Bye. Bye. Bye. Bye. Bye. Bye. Bye. Bye. Bye. Bye.
summary: ```markdown # Group Internal Lines | Clo 2025.1 Features Deep Dive ## Introduction Hey everyone, it's Phoebe here, and I have some great updates to share with you for our internal lines. So let's dive on in and have some fun while we learn. ## Improvements to Grouping Here I have my 2D window, and I'm going to show you some fun updates we have with our internal lines. The first thing is the improvement to grouping. With my transform pattern tool selected (shortcut **A**), I can select my two internal lines by holding down **Shift**, and then right-clicking right on top of them. You could always get to group, and then you can group the internal lines. But now we have that shortcut where you can just select these two, hold down **Shift**, and then hit **Control-G** (for Mac, it would be **Command-G**). Once you're done grouping, you can select your internal lines. Once they're selected and grouped, you can see that now you can move them around, and they'll all be grouped together. They will keep the grouping even if you decide to cut this right here. If I decide to cut this pattern, the grouping will still stay, as you can see. Even if I decide to re-merge this together, their grouping will stay. The only way that it's not going to group is if you select it, right-click, and ungroup them. Pretty cool! ## New Features with Center Line Now, another really cool update we've done with the internal lines is with the center line. Now you can extend it to that center line. Going to your **Edit Pattern** tool, you can then select the internal line, right-click right on top of it, and then choose **Extend to Trim**, and then you can say to **Unfolded Line**. It will extend to the Unfolded Line. You can see that there's only one internal line, and it's great. It will not work with **Add Point**. If I select this, right-click, and choose **Extend/Trim to Add Point**, it's not going to be there. That's because you cannot add a point to that center line, right? You can only add segment points to pattern outlines, and the center line is not a pattern outline. So that's why that doesn't work. It makes sense. However, you can, of course, go to **Extend/Trim**, and then to **Unfolded Line**. ## Distributing Internal Lines We also added this feature if you decide to distribute. If I go to my back pattern here and select these two pattern outlines, right-click on top, and select **Distribute Internal Line Between Segments**, I then have an option right here, **Extend to Unfolded Line**. This will extend to this half. I can then increase it, right? I can also specify that I want it to be a straight line or anything like that. After that, I can hit **OK**, and then the other one will be created. So really great and helpful! ## Conclusion Thanks for watching! For any questions, please use the comment section down below. Don't forget to like and subscribe. There are tons of great videos to help you out in your CLO journey. Keep having fun in CLO, and thanks again. Bye! ```
